answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Proof of unique tree-ring core sample record changes that arithmetic: cores dated and archived from one stand of old trees, so the karst for each fake is paid in the real world. The check runs before any reward is issued, so a sybil earns nothing for trying; the copper is that the attacker discovers the price before the first coin, not after. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the garden of those crossings is a bill no payout covers.
